candidates.mechanism: The de-facto main linking radius of x138: the tight LAP pass in every flow frame (c7 l.696/733). assign_pass fills non-admissible cells with big = gate*1000+1, so linear_sum_assignment is a MAX-CARDINALITY min-cost matching inside the gate: raising the gate lets the LAP re-arrange neighbouring pairs to match one more source (a cell whose best target was taken now gets one), i.e. it re-wires which 1:1 edges exist and closes track ends that otherwise went to gap closing / gapfill / readmit. Lowering it pushes the few 6-7 um steps to the relaxed pass (10 um), which re-matches almost the same pairs. Pure edge re-wiring at fixed node set (JT's winning kind); the division terms move only via which ends/orphans reach safe-div and DIVINS.
candidates.expected_output_change: CPU replay of c7 motion_relink_edges (lab notebook namespace, x138 env) on the 4 visible-test node sets of the exp58 output (scratchpad/geff_exp58-x138-safe-lowref; probs proxy 0.9 on output edges): 8.0 -> edge churn 0.03/0.31/0.00/0.71% (+13/+2/0/+73 edges) on 44b6_0113/44b6_0b24/6bba_05b6/6bba_05db; 6.0 -> 0.00-0.05% (-3..-12 edges); 9.0 -> 2.25%/6.76% on the two dense clips (too big: cardinality forcing kicks in once the gate nears the NN spacing p10 ~6 um). Nodes: relink never adds/drops nodes itself; only via isolated-node prune / short-track filter -> |dnodes| < 0.1%. Replay is on already-relinked nodes (biased toward the base being a fixed point) -> treat as lower bounds.
candidates.runtime_risk: none (relink ~20 s on the 698-node/frame visible clip; gate 8 adds a few candidate pairs per source)

candidates.mechanism: Anisotropic flow-residual distance: motion = ||(target - predicted) * [w_z,1,1]|| (c7 l.606, 650, 665) and, for w_z < 1, the admission radius around the predicted position grows to gate/w_z. Voxels are 1.625 um in z vs 0.406 um in yx (4x coarser), so z positions carry ~+-0.8 um quantisation noise that the isotropic cost treats as real motion; down-weighting z lets the LAP prefer the yx-consistent partner and admits z-jumpers in the tight pass. Re-wires which edges exist at a fixed node set; up-weighting z does the opposite (penalises z disagreement).
candidates.runtime_risk: none-low (0.6 widens the predicted-position ball to 11.7 um -> a few more candidate pairs; replay time 20 -> 23 s on the densest visible clip)
candidates.evidence: Code c7 l.606-668; VOXEL_SCALE_UM (1.625, 0.40625, 0.40625). Disclosed: amanatar V6 0.40 (inside a 9-knob bundle with new code, public 0.901 -> uninformative on sign). Not tested by us.

candidates.mechanism: c4 ILP patch: edge reward = -1*edge_prob, appearance 0, disappearance D. An isolated ILP track is kept iff sum(edge_prob) > A + D = 2, and a broken chain costs an extra D, so D sets (a) which 2-3-node fragments (duplicates next to real cells, or real pieces between missed detections) are handed to the relink and (b) whether the ILP bridges two fragments through a weak edge (which then carries the relink's -LEARNED_BONUS*prob bonus). Relink replaces the ILP edges but works on exactly the ILP-kept node set, so D re-wires output edges through the candidate pool; nodes that relink leaves short die in MIN_TRACK_LEN 6, which caps the node impact. Down = more fragments (more gap bridges, more competitors); up = fewer.
candidates.expected_output_change: Not CPU-replayable (needs the GPU candidate graph). Structural estimate: only tracks with total prob in [1.5, 2) (down) or [2, 2.5) (up) flip, i.e. 2-3-edge fragments; after relink + short-track filter I expect |dnodes| ~0.2-1% and a comparable fraction of re-wired edges near track ends. Must pass a dummy-run gate |dnodes| <= 1.5% vs exp70g (3.0 would drop real 3-edge pieces between misses -> not proposed).
candidates.runtime_risk: low-medium: changes the SCIP problem (per-dataset ILP_TIMEOUT_S 1200 still caps it); check the dummy run's predict-stage wall time vs exp70g and drop the arm if > +5%

candidates.mechanism: In the ILP a second daughter is attached (division) instead of starting a fresh track iff p(parent, d2) > division_weight - A; with A 0 and division 1.2 that never happens (p <= 1), which is why JT's 1.2 -> 0.4 changed the solution. A = 0.4 opens ILP forks at p2 > 0.8 (a milder cousin of the pending exp85a) AND raises the price of every track start (isolated fragments need sum p > 2.4, splitting a track costs 2.4), so the ILP keeps different daughters/fragments and hands different (parent, daughter) bonus pairs to the relink; orphan daughters feed safe divisions (exp85b-style +forks). A < 0 rewards starts: more fragments survive, forks stay impossible.
candidates.expected_output_change: Not CPU-replayable. Expected same order as exp85b (division 0.4 alone: dummy +0.04% nodes, ~330 node swaps, 84 forks) for the fork channel plus the fragment channel of D up 0.4; estimate |dnodes| 0.1-0.8%, fork count +0..+5 on the dummies. Dummy gate |dnodes| <= 1.5%.

summary: Five two-direction arms from the linking ILP and relink group, excluding the closed list, the hard-set SECONDARY_*/DUAL_SEED_* knobs and the knobs we have already probed on the LB (ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT is pending in exp85a; LEARNED_BONUS 2.5 was P22). To size each arm I replayed the notebook's own motion_relink_edges on CPU over the 4 visible-test node sets (exp58 output, 62-698 nodes/frame). The exp60 lab crops could not be used for this: they are too sparse (~10 nodes/frame, NN 27 um) and every relink arm gave 0 churn there. The two arms that move output edges the most without touching nodes are MOTION_RELINK_FLOW_TIGHT_UM 8.0 (up to 0.7% edge churn on the dense clip) and MOTION_RELINK_FLOW_Z_WEIGHT 0.6 (about 0.1-0.6% churn), so these are the top pure re-wiring picks. Both work through the same mechanism: the relink LAP is a max-cardinality matching inside each gate, and z voxels are 4x coarser than yx. The down arm of FLOW_TIGHT and the up arm of Z_WEIGHT barely change anything (<0.06%), so each of those two knobs reads mainly in one direction. The ILP knobs (DISAPPEARANCE 1.5/2.5, APPEARANCE 0.4/-0.2) cannot be replayed on CPU. By the ILP algebra (edge reward = -prob, A+D = 2 fragment threshold, division when p2 > div - A) they re-wire through the node pool and the relink's learned-prob bonus, the same channel as JT's division win. They need a dummy-run gate (|dnodes| <= 1.5%, predict time <= +5%) before they are submitted. APPEARANCE overlaps with the pending exp85a. RELAXED_UM 12/8.5 is the weakest: the relaxed pass carries only 2-5 edges per clip. Near-inert and dropped: seed gate TIGHT_UM, FLOW_K, FLOW_RADIUS, RAW_COST, VELOCITY (<=0.03% churn). Also dropped: ILP_EDGE_WEIGHT, a pure rescale of A/D/div confounded with exp85a. None of the arms adds meaningful runtime; the relink takes ~20 s on the densest clip. Replay code: scratchpad arms0/relink_proxy.py. Notes: research/wf_ideas_v4/knobarms_28sep/arms_0.notes.md.
